evals.prompt: Our support team wants KPIs. Prepare a session where they choose their own set — what should we measure?
assertions: Proposes at most 5 KPIs for the team, not a long menu adopted wholesale
Every proposed speed/volume KPI is explicitly paired with a quality counterpart
Each proposed KPI names a formula, a data source, an owner, and the decision it would change
Recommends inventorying what is already measured (existing dashboards/exporters) before defining anything new
Frames the session so the team chooses its own KPIs (timeboxed workshop, team ownership), not KPIs imposed on them

evals.prompt: Review our KPI list: deploys per week, story points completed, lines of code per developer, uptime, number of tickets closed. Is this a good set?
assertions: Flags lines of code per developer as an individual activity metric and advises against it, citing why individual productivity metrics mislead
Flags metrics that change no decision or invite gaming (Goodhart), such as story points completed or tickets closed as targets
Notes missing quality counterparts for the speed metrics (e.g. change failure rate or rework next to deploys per week)
Asks for or supplies the definition fields (formula, source, owner, target vs baseline) rather than judging names alone

evals.prompt: I want a dashboard with per-developer productivity metrics that managers can see.
assertions: Warns that individual productivity metrics are unreliable proxies (SPACE) and rankings damage collaboration
Requires explicit conditions before person-level visibility: the person sees the same data, purpose limited to coaching/workload (not appraisal), transparency about who sees what, and no leaderboards
Raises the EU/NL compliance angle: employee-monitoring rules (GDPR/AVG) and works-council consent where applicable
Offers a team-level or aggregated alternative as the default

evals.prompt: Measure the p95 latency of the /orders endpoint during the load test and tell me if it exceeds 300ms.
assertions: Performs the performance measurement without loading KPI-grooming guidance
